messages:
jordan: quick sync request  we need a hardened pattern for SIEM exports: retention tiers, who can request exports, and an emergency access playbook. Customers in finance/regulatory are pushing deadlines.
sam: +1. what's currently blocking? do we have RBAC to limit who can trigger exports? right now anyone with logs:read in project can kick them off which is too broad.
marta: agreed. I suggest 3 controls: 1) export trigger perms (export.request role), 2) export execution via ephemeral SA (no long lived creds), 3) export objects envelope-encrypted with per-export key.
leo: unwrap/forwarding is the hard part for downstream SIEMs. we can't expect Splunk ingestion to do KMS unwrap. we'd need an unwrap proxy that lives in our VPC with strict IAM and network controls.
jordan: unwrap-proxy is the design I want to standardize. key points: only accepts mutually TLS+IAM short lived certs, logs every unwrap to audit stream, exposes metrics so Console can alert on latency/errors.
sam: emergency access model? sometimes IR needs immediate reads during incidents and waiting for ticket approvals is too slow.
marta: emergency path should exist but be tightly audited: a one-time signed, timeboxed URL generated by an orchestrator after a 2-person approval that is recorded in the ticket system. TTL short (e.g., 15m) and the URL requires a rotated envelope key.
leo: fallback when unwrap-proxy in region is down: orchestrator should attempt cross-region unwrap via a standby proxy, and if that fails, generate the signed URL fallback. fallback issuance requires escalation and an audit push to Splunk.
jordan: for RBAC, minimal IAM for the ephemeral SA looks like this (pseudo):
```
role: roles/exports.runner
permissions: ["iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken", "storage.objects.create", "kms:Encrypt", "kms:Decrypt"]
condition: request.time < token.expiry
```
note: do NOT give logs.* read perms to this SA.
sam: good. also add a consumer-facing role for requesters: roles/exports.request that allows creating ExportRequest CRDs only. The controller handles the heavy lifting.
marta: retention tiers proposal: hot = 14d (indexable in Splunk), warm = 60d (nearline), cold-archive = 7y (for regulated customers). default pipeline: hot->warm->cold. evidence-hold pins to cold-archive and prevents auto-deletion.
leo: cost model needs to be in RFC. suggest customers can opt-in to extended retention for a fee. infra needs the ability to TTL by object metadata.
jordan: KMS notes: per-export ephemeral envelope keys encrypted under a customer-specific CMK. Rewrap flow when evidence-hold engages: call KMS.Rewrap to rewrap the envelope to the latest master key version. store rewrap ops in audit log.
sam: we must document compliance guardrails: creating service accounts with kms:Decrypt triggers an internal control check. security-bot, remind about policy CMP-7.
security-bot: [alert] policy CMP-7: service accounts with kms:Decrypt must be reviewed. Submit infra-exception ticket with justification if using broader decrypt scopes.
marta: operational runbook items:
- deploy/upgrade unwrap-proxy: healthchecks + canary in prod-west
- DR: standby proxy in prod-east with automated failover script
- metrics: unwrap_latency, unwrap_errors, unwrap_success_count
leo: also instrument the orchestrator: export_request_count, signed_url_issued_count, signed_url_approval_latency.
jordan: audit retention: keep unwrap and signed-url issuance logs for at least 2 years for forensics. index last 60 days in Splunk, archive full logs to bucket for 7 years.
sam: playbook snippet for incident response (short):
1) IR opens security ticket -> marks incident severity
2) If unwrap-proxy healthy: IR requests export via exports.request role -> approver workflow auto-grants ephemeral SA token -> unwrap-proxy returns logs to SIEM
3) If unwrap-proxy degraded: orchestrator attempts cross-region proxy -> if fails, request 2-person approval -> generate 15m signed URL -> notify oncall and log action
4) Post-incident: rotate envelope/master CMKs if key material exposure suspected and record rewrap ops
marta: include step to revoke any ephemeral tokens and rotate SA keys as part of postmortem if emergency fallback used.
leo: SLOs: unwrap-proxy p95 latency < 200ms, error rate < 0.1% over 24h. Console alert when any threshold breached.
jordan: I'll write RFC with diagrams (flow showing where audit logs go: Splunk index -> 60d + archive bucket -> longer term HSM/KMS audit trail). Will include the IAM snippets, runbooks, playbooks, and cost estimates.
security-bot: [info] linked compliance checklist template: https://redwood.internal/compliance/export-kms-checklist
jordan: thanks all. I'll ping back when draft RFC ready. tagging @sam @marta @leo for review :white_check_mark:
